newsitem.title: UK: Moody's may cut BT rating, affirms MCI.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may cut BT rating, affirms MCI.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had placed under review for possible downgrade the AAA senior debt ratings of British Telecommunications Plc (BT) and its guaranteed subsidiaries.
The short-term Prime 1 rating of BT is unaffected, Moody's said in a statement.
In addition, Moody's said it confirmed the A2 senior, A3 subordinated long-term, and Prime 1 short-term debt ratings of MCI Communications Corporation (MCI).

"The review of BT's ratings a prompted by the announcement that BT and MCI have entered into a merger agreement to create a global telecommunications company which will have a stronger competitive position but significantly higher debt leverage," Moody's said.
The new company will be called Concert Plc (Concert) and will have estimated revenues of about 25 billion stg serving 43 million customers in 70 countries, Moody's said.
Under the terms of the merger, MCI shareholders will own approximately 34 per cent of the fully diluted share capital of the new company, Moody's said.

In addition, they will receive from BT up to $3.8 billion in cash. BT will also pay in cash some 2.2 billion stg in the form of a special dividend to BT's existing shareholders, making BT's total cash payment amount to approximately 4.5 billion stg, Moody's said
"Moody's review will focus on whether the funding of this transaction will affect BT's future ability to sustain its very strong debt protection ratios," Moody's said.

"Moody's will also review the potential for additional investment needs to develop a more aggressive international strategy, at a time when competitive pressure is expected to increase in the UK," it said.
In addition, Moody's will analyse the operational and strategic benefits, as well as integration risk to result from the merger, it said.
"The proposed transaction could strategically reinforce the positions of both entities," it said.

"It could also leverage the strengths of both MCI and BT, to take full advantage of the opportunities emerging from the liberalization processes in both America and European telecommunications markets," Moody's said.

"Moody's confirmed the ratings of MCI because, although the merger could have positive implications for MCI at some point in the future, at this time it is not clear that the benefits would be sufficient to have ratings impact," it said.
MOODY'S SAID UNDER REVIEW FOR POSSIBLE DOWNGRADE ARE:
British Telecommunications Plc
--Eurobonds, zero coupon Eurobonds, unsecured loan stock, and counterparty rating at AAA.
British Telecom Finance BV
-- guaranteed Eurobonds and Euronotes at AAA.
British Telecom Finance Inc
-- guaranteed notes and debentures at AAA, and senior unsecured shelf registration at (P)AAA.

Moody's notes that the completion of the merger will take some time. There are a number of regulatory, tax and other approvals which need to be obtained in the UK, the US and Europe as well as the approval of BT's and MCI's shareholders," Moody's said.
